clue.text: Loudly lay into a lad, a worker, being rather flash?

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for playing loudly
to lam is to thrash or lay into someone
a lad is a boy
the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a young lad and a labourer, behaving in a showy way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flamboyant is showy and ostentatious, which is what flash means as an adjective.

clue.text: Some 'smoking makes one seethe

explanation.surface: Tobacco smoke infuriates a non-smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: A fume is a puff of smoke or vapour, some smoking; to fume is also to rage inwardly, to seethe.

clue.text: A king involved in a check-up is getting more ill-tempered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up inside another, as something involved in an affair sits within it
in a down clue the word for check is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rein is a check or restraint
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A monarch caught up in a medical check-up grows crosser.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'check-up' hides the split: 'check' supplies the word and 'up', in a down clue, sends it upwards. The king sits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Angrier is the comparative of angry, so it means more bad-tempered or irate.

clue.text: British shortfall reported in producing fruit

parts.note: a shortfall is a lack

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: 'in' meaning fashionable or up to date is current

explanation.surface: A British deficit is announced in fruit production.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'in producing' a phrase; 'in' is the word sounded, and 'producing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackcurrant is a small dark berry grown on bushes, an example of soft fruit.

clue.text: Make American alter any price raised in Kentucky

indicators.note: to alter the word any is to change the order of its letters
the raised price sits within the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a fee is a price paid

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper in Kentucky changes prices upward to Americanise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alter' rearranges the first word; in a down clue 'raised' reads the price upwards, and 'in' sits that inside the state's postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: To yankeefy is to Americanise, Yankee being slang for a US citizen.

clue.text: Form of tenure giving no indication of sex

indicators.note: a new form of the word tenure is a reshaping of its letters

explanation.surface: A type of land tenure is described as gender-neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Neuter is the grammatical gender that is neither masculine nor feminine, so it shows no sex.

clue.text: Left very short

indicators.note: short means the word for very is cut off before its end

parts.note: quite can mean very, as in quite right

explanation.surface: Someone departed after a very brief stay.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit is to depart, so having quit means having gone away.

clue.text: Need for speedy action in expedition

explanation.surface: Haste is required on a journey of exploration.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgency is pressing need to act quickly; expedition in its old sense means promptness or haste, the same quality.

clue.text: South hadn't moved the slightest bit

indicators.note: letters that have moved are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone from the South did not budge even a little.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in hadn't is ignored; its six letters join SOUTH for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth is one part in a thousand, a tiny fraction.

clue.text: Black eye almost confines one with a bit of a headache

indicators.note: one piece shuts the other in, as a cell confines a prisoner
almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a mouse is slang for a black eye
I is the Roman numeral for one
a grain is a tiny bit

explanation.surface: A bruised eye keeps someone in with a mild headache.
explanation.walkthrough: A mouse is old slang for a black eye; 'almost' drops its last letter before 'confines' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Migrainous is the adjective for migraine, a severe recurring headache.

clue.text: Commission a bit of adagio dancing

indicators.note: only a short run of letters from the words is wanted, a small part of them

explanation.surface: A ballet company is commissioned to perform part of a slow dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An agio is the fee or premium charged for exchanging currency, a commission.

clue.text: Commuters' leader sprinting over bridge to the station

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: haring means running fast, like a hare
to bridge something is to cross it

explanation.surface: The first commuter races across a bridge to catch a train.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARING CROSS is a main-line railway terminus in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Charing Cross is a London railway terminus, so it is a station by name.

clue.text: Result of having too much tipple shaken, not (at first). stirred?

definitions.text: Result of having too much tipple shaken, not (at first). stirred?

indicators.note: stirring a drink mixes it up, so the letters are mixed
only the opening letter of not is taken

explanation.surface: A Bond-style martini order, shaken not stirred, ends in seeing things after too much drink.
explanation.walkthrough: TIPPLE, SHAKEN and N (from 'not (at first)') are 'stirred' into a new order; the whole clue also describes the drunkard's visions.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing imaginary pink animals is the stock comic hallucination of someone very drunk.

clue.text: See 12
Author has a dig over Northern type of speech

definitions.note: the definition names a kind of speech, while the answer is the adjective describing a speaker of it

parts.note: H G Wells, the English novelist
a poke is a dig or prod

explanation.surface: A writer takes a jab at the way northerners talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-spoken describes refined, articulate speech, a particular kind of delivery.

clue.text: They may be warming up for the audition

definitions.text: They may be warming up for the audition

parts.words: They may be warming up for the audition
parts.note: reads as actors limbering up before trying for a part, but means things that keep the organs of hearing warm

explanation.surface: Performers loosen up before an audition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear-muffs are padded coverings worn over the ears for warmth.

clue.text: A picture of the children in colour

definitions.text: A picture of the children in colour

parts.words: A picture of the children in colour
parts.note: reads as a colour family photograph, but means a drawing made with the waxy stick children colour with

explanation.surface: A colour photograph of the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: A crayon is also a drawing done in coloured wax or chalk sticks, the medium children colour in with.

clue.text: One needs a way to follow up an account of the ball

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces come below, following up from the first

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed
I is the Roman numeral for one
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone needs a route to chase up a report about a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiard is the attributive form used for the game's equipment, as in a billiard ball.

clue.text: Charged a transport system for special clothing

parts.note: a live wire is electrically charged
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A rail network billed someone for uniforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Livery is the distinctive uniform worn by servants or members of a guild.

clue.text: Experienced doctor's near solution

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

indicators.note: a solution dissolves something, so the letters of near are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A seasoned physician is close to finding a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone with long experience; used here as an adjective, seasoned.

clue.text: Leo, perhaps, gets the job of director?

parts.note: Leo is one example of a sign of the zodiac
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A man called Leo is appointed to run the company.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer directs travellers, so it is cryptically a director.

clue.text: A fuller description of some figures

definitions.text: A fuller description of some figures

parts.words: A fuller description of some figures
parts.note: reads as a more detailed account of numbers, but means the label for larger body shapes

explanation.surface: A more complete account of some statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: Outsize is the clothing size for unusually large people, those with fuller figures.

clue.text: Dairy's early closure after half its product's gone off, getting high

indicators.note: only the front half of the word for the dairy's product is kept

parts.note: milk is what a dairy produces

indicators.note: the word closes early, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as the word dairy

explanation.surface: A dairy shuts early after half its milk goes sour, and someone gets high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone off' says the rest of the milk has disappeared; 'after' puts the clipped dairy second, and 'early closure' shuts that word one letter early.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in mid-air is up off the ground, aloft.

clue.text: Possible translation of Latin poet?

indicators.note: a translation renders words in another form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a classical poet could be translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Potential means latent or capable of coming into being.

clue.text: Losing a French accent that's charming?

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away

parts.note: the acute accent, accent aigu in French

explanation.surface: A Frenchman who drops his accent is thought charming.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means attractive in an endearing way.

clue.text: Not reported for' a bit of speeding?

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: these words are said aloud, and what is heard is the sound this part of the answer needs

explanation.surface: A minor speeding offence was never reported.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile per hour.

clue.text: 25's beginning to irritate the church

indicators.note: the beginning of the answer to 25 is its opening letter

parts.note: the answer to 25 Down, a unit of speed at sea
to irk is to irritate

explanation.surface: Something starts annoying the congregation.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is the answer to 25 Down, whose first letter is K. KIRK is the Scottish word for church.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirk is the Scots word for a church, and the Kirk is the Church of Scotland.

clue.text: With new generation gap, a nation is like part of America

indicators.note: a new generation of the letters is a fresh arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A country troubled by a generation gap resembles part of the Americas.
explanation.definitionFit: Patagonian means belonging to Patagonia, the southern tip of South America.

clue.text: Articles about a nurse

indicators.note: about here means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: an and an are two indefinite articles

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces are written about a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nana is a children's nurse or nanny, like the dog-nurse in Peter Pan.

clue.text: It's bright and shining, so I'm up to try the air

parts.note: in horse racing a jockey is said to be up when riding, so I'm up gives I ride
to scent is to sniff the air for a smell

explanation.surface: It is a bright day, so I'm going out for a breath of fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, 'X up' means jockey X is riding, so 'I'm up' is I RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridescent means gleaming with shifting rainbow colours, brightly lustrous.
